_comment: STATED RULES, HELD AGAINST THE MEASURED CORPUS. Run: node scripts/extract-reference.mjs --against design/rules/type-scale.rules.json

A rule lives here so it can be KILLED. Three were killed during the research that commissioned this harness, and the two that died are kept in this file rather than deleted from it — a deleted rule teaches nobody why it was wrong, and the same rule gets proposed again next quarter.
Every rule must carry a `statement` a person can disagree with. A rule with no statement is a threshold nobody chose.

rules.statement: adjacent steps in a type scale must differ by at least 1.125x
rules.origin: scripts/design-probe.mjs MIN_STEP_RATIO — this repo enforces it today as a p2 finding
rules.expected: REFUTED — every reference with a +1 increment above 9px violates it by arithmetic, and that is most of them

rules.statement: a disciplined UI band uses no more than 6 distinct sizes
rules.origin: an orchestrator synthesis of 2026-08-28 that read mission-control's 6 sizes as restraint
rules.expected: a count cannot see near-duplicates; this rule passed mission-control's +0.5 ramp, which is what made it worth killing

rules.statement: a real interface has a display band above its UI band
rules.origin: a category error, stated so it can be checked
rules.expected: HELD across the captured corpus — and this rule's death is the one finding in the file that DID NOT SURVIVE re-measurement. It was killed on the evidence that play.grafana.org 'ships 12 14 and nothing else', which reproduces exactly WITHOUT a scroll pass and is false WITH one: scrolled, grafana renders 15.4/16.8/18.2/28 above its UI band. So the rule that was declared a category error is currently HELD by 5 of 5 references. Reproduce both readings: `--no-scroll` against `--scroll` (the default). The lesson is not that the rule is right; it is that a rule killed on one measurement dies again or lives again when the instrument improves, and this file is where that gets noticed.

rules.statement: every adjacent increment in the UI band is a whole number of pixels
rules.origin: the observation this harness was built to test: five references build the UI band on +1 or +2, while mission-control uses +0.5 repeatedly
rules.expected: HELD across the captured corpus, and VIOLATED by mission-control — which is the finding, not a bug in the rule

rules.statement: UI-band increments are +1 or +2 and nothing else
rules.origin: the stronger form of the rule above
rules.expected: unknown — this is the one in the file whose answer was not decided before it was run

rules.statement: every adjacent increment in the UI band is a whole number of pixels, counting only sizes the reference renders at least 3 times
rules.origin: the same rule as ui-increments-are-integer, restated over sizes that carry real text. Both are kept BECAUSE THEY DISAGREE: play.grafana.org renders 12.6px on exactly one element, which is enough to violate the unfiltered form and not enough to mean anything about grafana's system. Which of the two is the real rule is a judgement, and the harness's job is to make the two answers visible rather than to pick one.
rules.expected: differs from ui-increments-are-integer on at least one reference; if it never does, one of the two is redundant and should be deleted
